name: Push-Up
summary: A bodyweight press that trains the chest, shoulders, triceps and trunk, scalable by changing the hand height or adding load.
setup: Place hands on the floor slightly wider than shoulder width, fingers spread.
Extend your legs behind you, feet together or hip-width.
Squeeze glutes and brace abs so the body forms a straight line from head to heels.
Position hands under the shoulders or slightly lower; screw them into the floor.
execution: Lower your body as one unit, elbows about 45 degrees from the torso.
Touch the chest close to the floor while keeping the body straight.
Push the floor away to return to the start.
Keep the neck neutral, looking slightly ahead of the hands.
mistakes: Hips sagging or piking: squeeze glutes and brace the abs, or elevate the hands.
Elbows flared to 90 degrees: tuck them to about 45 degrees.
Partial range of motion: lower until the chest is near the floor or use an incline to keep full range.
Head dropping forward: keep the neck in line with the spine.
